title: Founding of Rome
description: By the Roman tradition Romulus founds the city on the Palatine Hill; archaeology shows settlement there from about this time.

title: Roman Republic founded
description: The Romans expel their last king, Tarquin the Proud, and replace the monarchy with elected magistrates.

title: Battle of Cannae
description: Hannibal surrounds and destroys a much larger Roman army, the worst defeat in Roman history, yet Rome fights on.

title: Carthage destroyed
description: At the end of the Third Punic War the Romans raze Carthage and make its land the province of Africa.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
description: Senators stab Caesar to death at a meeting of the Senate, setting off the civil wars that end the Republic.

title: Battle of Actium
description: Octavian's fleet defeats Mark Antony and Cleopatra, leaving him sole ruler of the Roman world.

title: Octavian becomes Augustus
description: The Senate grants Octavian the name Augustus, the conventional beginning of the Roman Empire.

title: Eruption of Vesuvius
description: The eruption buries Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash; the traditional date is 24 August, though evidence points to the autumn.

title: Edict of Milan
description: The emperors Constantine and Licinius agree to tolerate Christianity throughout the empire.

title: Sack of Rome by the Visigoths
description: Alaric's Visigoths plunder the city, the first time in about 800 years that Rome falls to a foreign enemy.

title: Last western emperor deposed
description: Odoacer removes the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus, the conventional end of the Roman Empire in the west.

title: Lombards invade Italy
description: The Lombards under Alboin cross the Alps and take most of northern Italy from the Byzantines.

title: First doge of Venice
description: By Venetian tradition the lagoon communities elect Paolo Lucio Anafesto as their first doge; his existence is doubted.

title: Battle of Legnano
description: The cities of the Lombard League defeat Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, securing their self-government.

title: Sack of Constantinople
description: The Fourth Crusade, carried by the Venetian fleet, takes and loots the Byzantine capital, and Venice gains an empire in the eastern Mediterranean.

title: Black Death reaches Sicily
description: Galleys from the Black Sea bring the plague to Messina, from where it spreads through Italy and Europe.

title: Venice defeats Genoa at Chioggia
description: The surrender of the Genoese fleet in the lagoon decides the long rivalry between the two republics in Venice's favour.

title: Cosimo de' Medici returns to Florence
description: Recalled from exile, the banker Cosimo becomes the unofficial ruler of Florence, and his family dominates the city for most of three centuries.

title: Peace of Lodi
description: Milan and Venice end their war, and the main Italian states keep a balance of power for forty years.

title: Sistine Chapel ceiling completed
description: Michelangelo finishes the ceiling frescoes commissioned by Pope Julius II.

title: Sack of Rome
description: Mutinous troops of Emperor Charles V storm and loot Rome, an event often taken to end the High Renaissance.

title: Galileo condemned
description: The Inquisition finds Galileo vehemently suspect of heresy for holding that the Earth moves round the Sun, and he recants.

title: Fall of the Republic of Venice
description: Under threat from Napoleon the Great Council votes the republic out of existence after about 1,100 years.

title: Five Days of Milan
description: An uprising drives the Austrian garrison from Milan and starts the First Italian War of Independence.

title: Garibaldi lands at Marsala
description: Giuseppe Garibaldi and his thousand volunteers land in Sicily and go on to conquer the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

title: Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
description: Parliament proclaims Victor Emmanuel II of Sardinia king of a united Italy, still without Venice and Rome.

title: Capture of Rome
description: Italian troops breach the walls at Porta Pia, ending the Papal States and completing unification.

title: Battle of Adwa
description: The Ethiopian army of Menelik II defeats an Italian invasion, keeping Ethiopia independent.

title: Italy enters the First World War
description: Italy declares war on Austria-Hungary, having been promised territory by the Allies in the Treaty of London.

title: Battle of Caporetto
description: An Austro-German offensive breaks the Italian front and drives it back to the Piave.

title: March on Rome
description: Fascist blackshirts converge on the capital, and the king asks Benito Mussolini to form a government.

title: Lateran Treaty
description: Italy and the Holy See settle the dispute left by 1870, and Vatican City becomes an independent state.

title: Italy enters the Second World War
description: Mussolini declares war on France and Britain as France is collapsing.

title: Fall of Mussolini
description: After the Allied landing in Sicily the king dismisses and arrests Mussolini.

title: Armistice announced
description: Italy's surrender to the Allies, signed at Cassibile five days earlier, is made public, and German forces occupy the north and centre.

title: Italians vote for a republic
description: A referendum abolishes the monarchy, and women vote in a national poll for the first time.

title: Treaty of Rome
description: Italy, France, West Germany and the Benelux countries found the European Economic Community.

title: Aldo Moro kidnapped
description: The Red Brigades seize the former prime minister and kill him after 55 days.

title: Capaci bombing
description: The Mafia kills the anti-Mafia judge Giovanni Falcone, his wife and three police officers.
